recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is for FHIR-10205. If FHIR-I resolves FHIR-54050 or another follow-up about cpb-4 wording or semantics, handle that as a separate issue rather than reopening the DSTU2 cardinality request.
issue_request: FHIR-10205 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-core Conformance issue asking to change Conformance.rest from 0..* to 0..2 because the then cnf-8 invariant allowed only one REST declaration per mode.
initial_application: The Jira application comment says svn revision 14121 revoked the one-rest-per-mode constraint after discussion, rather than tightening cardinality, because the rest element definition allowed multiple client/server or configuration-setting repetitions. The current in-scope successor resource is CapabilityStatement, where rest remains 0..* with that multiple-repetitions comment.
additional_context: FHIR-33955 is a later Published/Persuasive R5 issue for the same artifact that explicitly requested adding an invariant so CapabilityStatement.rest has only one repetition per mode. Its linked Zulip discussion says there should only be one client and one server repetition and suggests an invariant because the resource design could not express cardinality 0..2. Commit 071000dbe2 added cpb-4. FHIR-54050 is only Triaged/Unresolved and questions wording, not a final contrary decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active source already matches the later FHIR-33955 decision by keeping CapabilityStatement.rest max=* and enforcing rest.mode.isDistinct() through cpb-4; changing max to 0..2 or removing cpb-4 for FHIR-10205 would conflict with later final history.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 decision that deliberately reintroduced the one-rest-per-mode invariant for CapabilityStatement.rest.
Triaged unresolved R6 ballot issue about cpb-4 wording; not a final decision for this reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: The 2018 thread agreed to revoke the invariant and allow rest to repeat 0..* for endpoint/configuration use cases.
